papers.title: Integrating physiology, transcriptomics and phylogenomics reveals the adaptive evolution of biennial fruiting in angiosperms.
papers.journal: Plant science : an international journal of experimental plant biology
papers.abstract: Most angiosperms complete fruit maturation within a single growing season, but a few lineages require two. However, the physiological and molecular mechanisms underlying this prolonged fruit development (PFD), and whether it represents a shared ancestral trait or a convergent adaptation, remain unresolved. Here we investigate 2-year fruiting species in Fagaceae, Rhamnaceae and Tapisciaceae, using morphological, histochemical, transcriptomic and phylogenomic approaches. The results show that fruits enter dormancy in autumn, resume growth in spring, and accumulate sugars and lipids during overwintering, indicating cold acclimation via starch/sucrose and fatty acid metabolism. Transcriptomic and co‑expression network analyses reveal that phytohormone (ABA, ethylene, auxin) and MAPK signaling are intertwined with sugar metabolism, forming a regulatory hub that controls dormancy. Crucially, by integrating phylogenomic dating across multiple lineages, we demonstrate that PFD did not arise from a common ancestor but evolved convergently, with the divergence of major PFD-bearing clades (Fagaceae, Rhamnaceae, Tapisciaceae) clustering near the Eocene-Oligocene boundary-a period of profound global cooling. Our findings provide a mechanistic and evolutionary framework for understanding PFD as a convergent adaptive strategy, linking molecular regulation of winter dormancy to deep-time climatic change.

papers.title: Effects of Partner Distress and Controlling Responses on Back Pain in Daily Life.
papers.abstract: Chronic back pain is embedded within close relationships, yet little is known about how partners' emotional and behavioral responses shape patients' daily pain experiences. This study examined whether partners' distress predicts their attempts to control (increase or decrease) the activity level of individuals with chronic back pain (ICBPs), and whether these responses are associated with worse subsequent pain outcomes the following day. One hundred forty-seven couples in which one partner had chronic back pain completed twice-daily electronic diary assessments for 30 days. The sample was older (70s), predominantly White, and well-educated. Partners reported daily pain-related distress and ICBPs reported partners' solicitousness (e.g., excessive help) and activity-related pressure. Multilevel models tested daily within- and between-couple associations and prospective next-day effects on pain severity, catastrophizing, and interference. As predicted, on days when partners experienced greater distress about ICBPs' pain, ICBPs reported more partner solicitousness (estimate =.234, SE =.037, p <.001; effect size =.799) and greater activity-related pressure (estimate =.033, SE =.017, p =.048; effect size =.524). In turn, greater partner solicitousness predicted higher pain catastrophizing (estimate =.050, SE =.021, p =.020; effect size =.098) and pain interference (estimate =.065, SE =.030, p =.028; effect size =.066) the following morning, controlling for prior-day pain outcomes. Contrary to prediction, activity-related pressure did not predict next-day pain severity, catastrophizing or interference. Partners' distress may contribute to behavioral responses in daily life, particularly excessive assistance, that inadvertently worsen pain-related functioning. PERSPECTIVE: Partners may experience emotional distress as a result of their loved one's pain. This distress may lead to behaviors that compromise the ability to cope effectively with pain. papers.title: Word-color association from large-scale online data: Methodology and applications.
papers.abstract: Words and colors are intimately associated in humans, a sign of the close relationship between verbal, linguistic expression and cognition. Word-color association therefore plays an important role in areas of communication such as marketing and literature. Traditional efforts to build a general, scalable, and quantitative mapping of word-color association have often relied on surveys, experiencing difficulties in curating large-scale data sets, enrolling sufficient participants, and excising potential inherent researcher biases in the choice of the words and the colors to be mapped. Even the most recent computational efforts based on Large Language Models (LLMs) do not overcome these problems due to their near-complete lack of transparency in data and methodology that results in low confidence, consistency, and reliability. Here we propose a framework that overcomes these limitations via the use of freely accessible large-scale web image data, and fully transparent and reproducible methods that allow one to build color associations for almost any given word. We also showcase the methodology in action through analyses of color usage in corporate branding and 20th-century Anglo-American poetry. These show that our framework can help form new answers to and perspectives on long-standing questions in communication. Additionally, our framework by design can be readily adopted for use in any language supported by a web image search engine, and its code is freely available in open source; we therefore expect it to contribute towards achieving a universal, multilingual understanding of word-color association.

papers.title: Ternary interactions of polyphenols, polysaccharides, and gluten proteins: molecular mechanisms and strategic regulation of flour-based product quality: a review.
papers.abstract: As a major staple, wheat supplies 18% of global dietary energy and 19% of protein. Wheat flour-based foods constitute complex matrices wherein gluten, starch, non-starch polysaccharides, polyphenols, and water undergo dynamic interactions during sequential processing. Integrating findings from binary and ternary systems, this comprehensive review identifies hydrogen bonding, hydrophobic interactions, water competition, macromolecular crowding, and covalent cross-linking as key driving mechanisms. Depending on formulation, these interactions govern gluten network development, starch transitions, and water mobility, thereby shaping product volume, texture, sensory quality, and glycemic response. Reversible association dominates mixing, thermal aggregation dictates baking, and moisture migration coupled with retrogradation governs storage stability. Overall, non-covalent, water-mediated effects predominate over the formation of distinct ternary complexes in intact dough. This review establishes a structure-processing-quality framework linking molecular-level interactions across sequential processing stages to the macroscopic quality and nutritional functionality of flour-based foods.

papers.title: Sense-antisense RNA duplexes mediate stress-responsive translational control in Plasmodium falciparum.
papers.abstract: Plasmodium falciparum, the primary cause of human malaria, relies on tightly coordinated gene-expression programs to adapt to host-derived stress despite possessing a limited repertoire of canonical transcription factors. Antisense long noncoding RNAs have emerged as important regulators of parasite biology, including virulence gene regulation and sexual commitment; however, their prevalence, origin, and broader functional significance remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that antisense transcription is a widespread, reproducible, and regulated feature of the P. falciparum transcriptome rather than a by-product of pervasive euchromatic transcription. Environmental stress, including febrile temperature exposure and artemisinin treatment, extensively remodeled antisense transcription, particularly at loci associated with virulence and stress adaptation, promoting widespread sense-antisense RNA duplex formation. Functional analyses of two stress-responsive chromatin regulators, PfGCN5 and PfHDAC1, identified as antisense-expressing loci, revealed that increased antisense expression elevated steady-state mRNA abundance while reducing cognate protein levels. Mechanistically, sense-antisense RNA duplex formation stabilized complementary transcripts but suppressed translation. Integrated transcriptomic, RNA-RNA duplex profiling, ribosome sequencing, and proteomic analyses further showed that duplex-enriched transcripts exhibit reduced ribosome occupancy and reduced protein abundance, accompanied by localized antisense enrichment near transcription end sites and altered ribosome distribution consistent with impaired translational engagement. Collectively, our findings identify an antisense RNA-ribosome regulatory axis that couples RNA duplex formation to adaptive translational control, providing a previously unrecognized mechanism underlying stress adaptation and posttranscriptional gene regulation in P. falciparum.
